issue: After Dispatcher.call resolves successfully, response JSON encoding, per-response limit or shared retained-output admission can still throw. A response failure must not label the completed request not_sent. The original durable receipt remains authoritative.
method: Static independent review of complete two-file diff and surrounding GatewayServer.handle authentication/RPC/catch/finally flow, JSON writer, retained-response budget and release paths; existing Dispatcher acceptance/receipt boundary and errorBody defaults checked. No independent execution or resource exhaustion attempted.

Reviewed both new parameterized test bodies and real HTTP fixture. A real in-memory Ledger and actual Dispatcher rename commit precede one bounded injected writer error. Each test queries the original operation and confirms accepted/Saved; missing-project validation then proves true not_sent remains unchanged.
conclusions: rpcCompleted is initialized per request and set immediately after await Dispatcher.call succeeds, before JSON serialization/admission. Subsequent HarnessError and generic failures are forced unknown regardless of their default delivery.

Authorization, recovery-protocol, body parsing and actual Dispatcher rejection occur before the flag; existing explicit rejection/unknown semantics remain unchanged. Authentication-completion protection is preserved.

If headers are already sent or the error response also cannot acquire capacity, existing close/destroy path remains; no additional unbounded error body or false not_sent reply is introduced. Budget releases and backend/response settlement ordering are unchanged.
No receipt state is changed by the HTTP repair. Accepted operation remains recoverable by original identity rather than inviting a new mutation.
